overview.summary: Toki is an internal team chat for one company: channels, direct messages, threads and files, and later tasks, calendar, video meetings, a guest portal, automations, mail and AI summaries. Each company runs its own copy on its own server.

requirements.rulesIntro: Thirteen rules drawn from the prototype review. They apply to every phase.
requirements.assumptionsIntro: Sixteen product details set while writing the flows, confirmed on 12 Nov 2026.

rules.text: No feature may be hover-only or desktop-only. Every action has an entry point on narrow and touch screens.

Smallest supported size is 360 × 560. Under 720px: one pane at a time. From 720 to 1099px: side panels (thread, details, profile) overlay the chat instead of squeezing it. From 1100px: three columns. Navigation and the tab row scroll when short of room; the conversation list is always the main area of the sidebar.

A reversible action happens at once and shows a toast with Undo for 5 seconds. An irreversible action, or one that affects other people, asks for confirmation and names its target. Never both for one action.
A form that has content does not close on an outside click; closing it by button asks whether to discard.
Your own action never notifies you. An Activity item becomes done on its own once the thing it asks for is done. Activity is newest first and has a filter chip for every kind of item.

During Pause or Focus time there is no toast, push or sound, including reminders you set yourself. Badges still update. When it ends, one summary lists what arrived. Starting Focus during Focus extends it rather than nesting; ending restores the earlier status.

Dates and times: required fields cannot be left empty; where a future time is needed the past is rejected; the year is shown whenever it is not the current year; one format across the app; 'Invalid Date' never appears.
Every searchable or filterable list has an empty state centred in the content area and written for that context. A count on a chip always equals the rows shown.
Every icon-only button has a name for screen readers (lint checks it). A modal traps focus and returns it to the opening button. Menus work with arrow keys.
After something is created, the screen shows it; if a filter would hide it, the filter changes.
Writing to a conversation (sending, starting a Meet, scheduling) requires membership. Pickers list only conversations you have joined.
Toasts and floating bars never cover the composer or navigation.

When the connection drops: loaded content stays readable; messages being sent wait and send themselves when the connection returns; every other action is blocked with an explanation, never a false success.

assumptions.text: Every workspace has a #general channel created at setup; every member is in it automatically; it cannot be left or archived.
The app opens on the conversation last viewed on that device; the first time, on #general.
Presence turns to Away after 5 minutes without activity. There is no separate Offline state.
An invitation expires after 7 days. The link in the invitation signs the person in directly, without a code.
At most 5 code requests per email in 15 minutes; the resend button enables after 60 seconds.
There can be several Owners. The last Owner cannot be demoted or deactivated.
Channel names: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, up to 80 characters, unique. Public cannot become private after creation, or the reverse.
Any channel member can edit the topic and use @channel; in a channel of 20 or more people, @channel asks for confirmation first.
A message holds up to 10,000 characters and 10 files.
Deleting a message also removes its attached files from storage.
A push notification shows the sender, the conversation and the start of the message.
People cannot be added to or removed from a group DM.
Default notification level: 'Mentions only' for channels, 'All messages' for DMs.
Admins and Owners do not automatically see private channels or DMs; deleting messages, removing people and archiving apply only where they are members.
Toki has no 'seen' receipts; a sender does not know who has read a message.
A message deleted by an admin shows as 'Message deleted by an admin' and its author is told.

flowsIntro: Each flow says what the person does and what they see at every step, followed by other cases and what other people see. The 43 phase 1 flows are written in full; the 8 later-phase flows are outlines to be detailed when that phase is planned.

flows.title: First-time workspace setup
flows.context: The server was just installed and the database is empty. Environment variables hold the first admin's email and name, and the workspace name.
steps: The server starts, finds no accounts, and creates the workspace, the Owner account and the #general channel.
The Owner opens Toki's address and sees the sign-in page with the workspace name.
The Owner signs in with a code, as in F04.
On first entry the Owner sees Home with an empty #general, the line 'This is the start of #general', and a card suggesting three things: invite members, create a channel, set a status.
cases: A required environment variable is missing: the server does not start and prints the name of the missing variable.
The database already has accounts: the setup variables are ignored; nothing is created or changed.
Mail cannot be sent: the Owner gets a one-time sign-in link from a server command (F43).

flows.title: Invite members
flows.context: On the Admin page.
steps: Press 'Invite members'. The modal has an email field (several addresses, separated by commas or new lines) and a role picker, Member by default.
Press 'Send invitations'. Each valid address becomes a row in the member table with status 'Invited', the date and who invited them.
Toki emails each address. Toast: '3 invitations sent'.
An 'Invited' row has two buttons: 'Resend' and 'Revoke'.
cases: Malformed email: the field shows an error underneath and that address is not sent; valid ones still go.
The email is already a member or already invited: it says 'already in the workspace' or 'already invited on …'; no duplicate is created.
An Admin can invite only as Member. An Owner can invite as Admin or Owner too.
An invitation expires after 7 days: the row turns to 'Expired' and keeps 'Resend'.
Revoke asks for confirmation; the link in the old email stops working.

flows.title: Accept an invitation and enter for the first time
flows.context: An invitation email is in the inbox.
steps: The email names the workspace and the inviter, and has a 'Join' button.
Pressing it opens Toki and signs the person in directly, with no code, because the link already proves control of that email.
A one-time welcome screen asks for a display name and job title; time zone and language come from the device and can be changed.
Press 'Enter Toki'. The newcomer lands on Home, already in #general, with its full history.
#general shows a system line, 'Minh joined'. The Admin page changes the person's status to 'Active'.
A small card asks whether to turn on notifications (F36).
cases: The link was already used: it goes to the normal sign-in page with the email filled in.
The link expired or was revoked: the page says why and suggests contacting the inviter.
Skipping the welcome screen: the display name is the part of the email before the @, editable later in Preferences.

flows.title: Sign in
flows.context: Already a member, with no session on this device.
steps: Open Toki and see the sign-in card: logo and workspace name, an email field, a 'Send code' button.

Enter the email and press 'Send code'. The screen changes to 'Check your email': it repeats the address, shows a 6-digit field, the line 'The code works for 10 minutes', a 'Use a different email' link, and a 'Resend code' button that enables after 60 seconds.
The email arrives with a 6-digit code and a sign-in button.
Type the code (all 6 digits can be pasted; it submits when complete) or press the button in the email.
Home opens. The session lasts 30 days and renews on every use.
cases: The email button is pressed on a different device from the one that asked for the code: that device is signed in; the other still waits for the code.
A valid session already exists: opening Toki goes straight to Home, with no sign-in page.

flows.title: Sign-in errors
flows.context: On the sign-in page. Each error appears under the field, in words that say what to do next.
steps: Email not in the workspace: the screen still moves to 'Check your email' as usual and no email is sent. The page never reveals which emails are members.
Wrong code: the field shakes slightly and says 'That code is not right. 4 tries left.'
Five wrong tries: the code is cancelled, 'This code is locked. Ask for a new one.'
Code older than 10 minutes: 'This code has expired', with a 'Send a new code' button.
More than 5 code requests in 15 minutes: 'You have asked for too many codes. Try again in 12 minutes.'
Deactivated account: after a correct code, 'This account has been deactivated. Contact an admin.'
Network lost while sending: the button becomes pressable again, 'Could not connect. Check your network and try again.'

flows.title: Sign out and manage sessions
flows.context: Signed in.
steps: Press the account card at the bottom of the sidebar (narrow screens: the More sheet). The menu has Set status, Pause notifications, Focus time, Preferences, Sign out.
Press 'Sign out': unsynced drafts are saved to the server, this device's session is ended, its push registration is removed, and the sign-in page appears.
Preferences has a 'Signed-in devices' section: each row shows the device kind, browser and last use; the current one is labelled 'This device'.
Press 'Sign out' beside another device, or 'Sign out all other devices'; both ask for confirmation.
cases: Once every device is signed out, other people see the person as Away.
A device signed out remotely: see F07.

flows.title: Session expires or is revoked while in use
flows.context: Using the app when the session expires or is ended from another device.
steps: The server refuses the next request and closes the realtime connection.
The app shows 'Your session has ended' with a 'Sign in again' button; the content behind is covered.
After signing in again the app returns to the conversation that was open. The draft being typed is still in the composer.
cases: Deactivated while in use: the same screen, but it says 'This account has been deactivated' and has no sign-in button.

flows.title: Open the app: the Home view
flows.context: Signed in.
steps: A skeleton of the layout appears at once; real data replaces it when loaded (target under 2 seconds).

Calm look: the left sidebar holds the workspace name and head count, the Search field (Ctrl K), the items Home, Activity, Later, Files, People, Admin (Admins and Owners only), the conversation list, and the account card at the bottom. Focus look: a narrow icon rail and a separate conversation column.
Each navigation item has a badge: Home is total unread across unmuted conversations; Activity is unread items; Later is reminders that have come due.
The main area opens the conversation last viewed on this device; the first time, #general.
If that conversation has unread messages it scrolls to the 'New' divider; otherwise it sits at the bottom.
The account card shows the avatar, presence dot, name, and status or role.
cases: Narrow screens: Home is the full-screen conversation list; tapping a row opens the conversation. Bottom tabs: Home, Activity, Later, Files, More.
The last-viewed conversation was archived or left: #general opens.
In Pause or Focus: a strip at the top of the main area shows the end time and an end-early button.
No connection at open: a 'Reconnecting' strip shows and the app retries on its own.

flows.title: The conversation list
flows.context: On Home.
steps: Three collapsible groups: Starred, Channels, Direct messages. An empty group is not shown.
A channel row: # (public) or a lock (private), then the name. A DM row: avatar with presence dot, then the name. A group DM: a group icon and the members' names.
A row with unread messages has a bold name and a count on the right. With a mention it adds a red @ dot. A muted conversation is grey, shows no count, and still shows the @.
A conversation with an unsent draft that is not open has a 'Draft' label.
Three filter chips: All, Unread, Mentions. The search field filters by name.
Two buttons at the top: Browse channels and New message. A 'Browse channels' row closes the list.
cases: A filter matches nothing: 'No conversations match' and a 'Clear filter' button.
Order within a group: channels alphabetically; DMs by most recent message.
Collapsed groups and the filter are remembered per device.

flows.title: Open and read a conversation
flows.context: Press a row in the list.
steps: The header shows: icon, name, a star if starred, the topic (for a DM, the other person's status or job title and presence), a search-in-conversation button, and a members button with the head count.
The tab row: Messages, Files & links, Pinned.

The message list has day dividers ('Yesterday', 'Today', or a full date). Consecutive messages from one person within 5 minutes are grouped: only the first has an avatar and name; hovering a grouped message shows its time in the margin.
With unread messages, the 'New' divider sits above the first unread one and the view scrolls there.
Once scrolled to the bottom with the window in use, the conversation counts as read. The row's count disappears and the Home badge drops, on all of the person's devices.
The 'New' divider stays put until the conversation is left; it is gone the next time.
Scrolling to the top loads older messages; the reading position does not jump.
cases: New messages arrive while scrolled up: a floating '↓ 3 new messages' button (with @ if one is a mention). Pressing it goes to the bottom.
An empty conversation: 'This is the start of #name. Say hello.'
Opened from a link to one message: it scrolls there and flashes for 2 seconds.
A link to a private channel the person is not in: 'You do not have access to this conversation', without revealing the channel name.
A link to a public channel not yet joined: a read-only preview with a 'Join' button.
An archived channel: readable; the composer is replaced by 'This channel has been archived'.

flows.title: Send a message
flows.context: A conversation the person belongs to is open.
steps: Type in the composer (placeholder 'Message #name'). Enter sends, Shift+Enter makes a new line. The field grows to 160px, then scrolls.
Others in the conversation see 'Lan is typing…' under the list; it clears after 5 seconds without typing.
Press send: the message appears at the bottom at once, slightly faded while the server confirms. The composer empties and keeps focus.
The server confirms: the message becomes solid.
Others with the conversation open see it appear immediately. Others see the row turn bold and its count rise.
cases: Send fails on the network: the message gets a 'Not sent' label with 'Retry' and 'Delete'. When the connection returns the app retries once on its own.
Empty or whitespace only: the send button does nothing.
Over 10,000 characters: a counter appears near the limit; beyond it the send button is locked.
Mid-word while typing Vietnamese: Enter finishes the word and does not send.
Switching conversation before sending: the text becomes a draft, still there on return, and syncs to other devices.

flows.title: Formatting, emoji and mentions
flows.context: Writing a message.
steps: The toolbar under the composer: bold, italic, code, emoji, attach, mention. Selecting text and pressing bold wraps it in asterisks; once sent it shows as bold.
Type @ or press the mention button: a popup lists the conversation's members (avatar, name, presence dot, status) plus @channel. Keep typing to filter; it matches with or without diacritics.
Arrow keys choose, Enter or Tab inserts, Esc closes the popup.
Once sent, a mentioned name shows as a chip. On the mentioned person's screen the whole message has a yellow background.
Links become clickable; a preview card (title, description, site name) appears after a few seconds.
cases: @channel in a channel of 20 or more people asks 'Notify 34 people?' before sending.
@ followed by a name outside the conversation: no suggestion, the text goes as plain text, nobody is notified.
The sender can remove a link preview with the × on the card.
A guest does not see the @channel entry.

flows.title: Being mentioned in a channel
flows.context: Minh posts a message with @Lan in #project-launch. The table under Roles & States covers every situation; this is the typical flow when Lan has the app open in another conversation.
steps: In the conversation list the #project-launch row turns bold, its unread count rises, and a red @ dot appears.
The Home badge rises by 1. The Activity badge rises by 1.
A toast: 'Minh mentioned you in #project-launch', with the first 60 characters of the message and a 'View' button. It closes after 5 seconds. A sound plays if sound is on.
Pressing 'View' or the channel row opens #project-launch, scrolls to that message and flashes it; the message has a yellow background.
Once the message is on screen the @ dot and count clear, and the Activity item becomes read.
In Activity the item reads: Minh's avatar, 'Minh Trần mentioned you: …', the channel name, the time, and two buttons, Done and Snooze.
cases: Minh edits out @Lan or deletes the message: the Activity item is removed and the badges fall back.
A mention inside a thread reply: the channel's unread count does not rise but an @ dot appears; opening the Activity item opens the thread panel at that reply.
With @channel: every member except the sender gets the same, worded 'mentioned the channel'.
On Minh's side the message looks like any other. Minh cannot tell whether Lan has read it; Toki has no seen receipts.

flows.title: Threads
flows.context: Looking at a message in a conversation.
steps: Hover the message and press 'Reply in thread' (narrow screens: tap the message to show the action bar).
The side panel opens: the root message, a '3 replies' line, the replies, and a 'Reply in thread' composer.
Under the composer is a checkbox, 'Also send to #name'. If ticked, the reply also appears as a normal message in the channel.
Send the reply. Under the root message in the channel a line appears: avatars of up to 3 repliers, '3 replies', 'Last reply 09:11'. Pressing it also opens the thread.
The root author, everyone who replied and everyone mentioned follow the thread automatically. Each new reply gives them a thread item in Activity.
cases: Replies do not raise the channel's unread count.
From 720 to 1099px the thread panel overlays the chat. On narrow screens the thread is full screen with a Back button.
The root message is deleted: the thread stays, and the root becomes 'Message deleted'.
Threads are one level deep: there is no reply button inside a thread.
A thread has a shareable path that reopens the same thread.

flows.title: Reactions
flows.context: Looking at a message.
steps: Press the smile button on the message's action bar: a panel of 8 emoji.
Pick one: a chip with the emoji and the count 1 appears under the message, outlined in the accent colour because it is yours.
Press that chip again to remove it. Press someone else's chip to add the same emoji.
Hovering a chip shows the names of those who reacted.
The message's author gets a reaction item in Activity, with no toast or push.
cases: One of each emoji per person per message; several different emoji are allowed.
Reacting to your own message creates no Activity item.

flows.title: Edit and delete your own message
flows.context: Looking at a message you sent.
steps: The 'More' menu on your own message has Edit and Delete.
Edit: the text becomes a field in place, with Save and Cancel; Enter saves, Esc cancels. After saving, '(edited)' shows beside the time.
Delete: a confirmation line appears under the message, 'Delete this message?', with Delete and Cancel.
After deleting: a message with no replies disappears for everyone. A message with replies becomes a 'Message deleted' line and its thread stays.
cases: Files attached to a deleted message are removed from storage and from Files.
Editing to add a mention notifies the newly mentioned person. Removing a mention removes the earlier notification.
There is no time limit on editing and no edit history.
Admins and Owners can delete other people's messages: see F42.

flows.title: Pin a message
flows.context: Looking at a message.
steps: 'More' → 'Pin to conversation'. A 'Pinned' label appears beside the sender. The toast offers Undo.
The channel shows a system line, 'Lan pinned a message'.
The 'Pinned' tab lists pinned messages, most recently pinned first. Pressing one jumps to it in the Messages tab.
Unpin from the same menu.
cases: Any member of the conversation can pin and unpin.
An empty tab: 'Nothing pinned. Pin a decision or a link so people can find it later.'

flows.title: Send files, images and links
flows.context: Writing a message.
steps: Press the paperclip, drag files onto the chat, or paste an image from the clipboard.
Each file becomes a small card above the composer: name, size, progress bar, an × button. Up to 10 files per message.
Sending is possible once every file has finished uploading.
In the message: images show as thumbnails that open large; other files show a card with icon, name and size.
Pressing a file card opens a detail modal with sender, conversation, date, size, and the buttons 'Open in conversation', 'Copy link', 'Download'.
The file appears in the conversation's 'Files & links' tab and in the Files section.
cases: A file over 100 MB: the card turns red, 'Over 100 MB', and is not uploaded.
An upload fails midway: the card gets a 'Retry' button.
A file link opens only for people who can see the conversation holding it.
A thumbnail not yet ready: a placeholder with the right proportions, so the layout does not jump.

flows.title: Search inside a conversation
flows.context: A conversation is open.
steps: Press the magnifier in the header: a search field appears under the tab row.
Type: the list keeps only messages containing the words or sent by someone whose name matches; typing without diacritics still finds text with them.
Press a result: search mode closes, the view scrolls to that message and flashes it.
Press × or Esc to close.
cases: No results: 'No messages match …'.

flows.title: Create a channel
flows.context: From 'Browse channels' → 'Create channel', or from Ctrl+K.
steps: The modal: Name (lower-cased automatically, spaces become hyphens), Topic (optional), a 'Private' switch, a field to add members.
Press 'Create'. The channel opens at once; you are its first member; a system line reads 'Lan created this channel'.
A public channel appears in everyone's 'Browse channels'. A private channel appears only to its members.
cases: The name already exists: an error under the field, even when it clashes with an archived channel.
Names use only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 80 characters.
A channel cannot switch between public and private after creation.

flows.title: Browse and join a public channel
flows.context: Press 'Browse channels'.
steps: The modal lists every public channel and the private ones you are in: name, topic, member count. It has a search field.
Joined channels have an 'Open' button; others have 'Join'.
Press 'Join': the channel opens with its full history and enters your list. Toast: 'Joined #name'.
The channel shows a system line, 'Lan joined'.
cases: Archived channels are listed with an 'Archived' label and only a 'View' button.
Nothing found: 'No channels match' and a 'Create channel' button named after the search text.

flows.title: Add people to a channel
flows.context: Open the channel's Details → 'Add people'.
steps: The search field lists only people not yet in the channel.
Choose one or more and press 'Add'.
Each added person sees the channel appear in their list, with an Activity item, 'Lan added you to #name'.
The channel shows a system line, 'Lan added Minh'.
cases: Any member can add people, in private channels too.
Added people see the full history.
Only Admins and Owners can remove someone from a channel, and only in channels they belong to.

flows.title: Leave a channel
flows.context: Details → 'Leave channel'.
steps: A public channel: you leave at once; the toast 'Left #name' offers Undo for 5 seconds. You can rejoin any time from Browse channels.
A private channel: a confirmation, 'Leave #name? A member will have to invite you back.' Undo is still offered for 5 seconds afterwards.
The channel leaves your list; the view moves to #general.
The channel shows a system line, 'Lan left the channel'.
cases: #general has no Leave button.
The last member leaving a private channel is warned: 'You are the last member. The channel will be archived.'
After leaving you get no more notifications; your old messages stay.

flows.title: Details, notifications, mute and star
flows.context: Press the members button in the header.
steps: The Details panel has: About (name, topic, description, creator, creation date), Members (avatar, presence, name, job title; press to open a profile), Notifications, Settings.
Notifications has three levels: All messages, Mentions only, Nothing. Defaults: 'Mentions only' for channels, 'All messages' for DMs.
The 'Mute' switch: the row turns grey, leaves the Home badge, and produces no toast or push.
The 'Star' switch: the conversation moves to the Starred group; a star shows in the header.
Edit the topic and description in place under About.
cases: Notification level, mute and star are personal and affect nobody else.
Any channel member can edit the topic and description; a change adds a system line.
For a DM the panel shows the other person's profile instead of Members.

flows.title: Direct messages and groups
flows.context: Press 'New message'.
steps: The modal has a field that searches people and channels.
Choose one person: the DM with them opens. If you have talked before, the same conversation reopens with its history.
Choose two to seven people: a group DM is created (8 people at most, counting you).
A DM appears in the other person's list only when the first message is sent.
The DM header shows the other person's avatar, presence, name, and status or job title.
cases: The same set of people always leads to the same conversation. People cannot be added to or removed from a group DM; for a different set, start a new group.
The other person is deactivated: history stays, and the composer is replaced by 'This account has been deactivated'.
The other person is in Pause or Focus: a line under the header reads 'Khoa has paused notifications until 14:00'. The message can still be sent.
Messaging yourself is not supported in phase 1.

flows.title: Archive a channel
flows.context: Details → 'Archive channel'. Only Admins and Owners who are members of the channel see the button.
steps: The confirmation names the channel and its member count.
Once archived: the channel leaves everyone's list, the composer is locked, and the history stays readable and searchable.
In Browse channels it carries an 'Archived' label. Admins and Owners have a 'Restore' button.
cases: #general cannot be archived.
Members with the channel open at that moment see a strip, 'This channel was just archived'.

flows.title: Activity
flows.context: Press Activity.
steps: The list is newest first. Each row: unread dot, the actor's avatar, a sentence, the conversation, the time.
Five kinds of item: you were mentioned; a reply in a thread you follow; a reaction to your message; you were added to a channel; an account change (role changed, message deleted by an admin).
Filter chips: All, Mentions, Threads, Reactions, Other, and 'Snoozed · n' when something is snoozed.
Press a row: it becomes read and opens the conversation at that message, or opens the thread.
Done removes the item, with Undo in the toast. Snooze offers 'In 1 hour', 'Today 15:00', 'Tomorrow 09:00'.
'Mark all read' sits at the top.
cases: A snoozed item leaves the main list; when due it returns to the top, unread, labelled 'Back from snooze', with a toast.
An empty list: 'You are all caught up' and an 'Open your conversations' button.
On touch devices Done and Snooze are always visible.
An item removes itself when its source message is deleted.

flows.title: Later and reminders
flows.context: Looking at a message to come back to.
steps: Press the bookmark on the message's action bar: toast 'Saved for Later' with a View button. The bookmark on that message changes colour.
Open Later. Two chips: In progress · n and Completed · n. Each row: a checkbox, the sender's avatar and name, the conversation, the start of the message, a 'Remind me' button.
'Remind me' opens a menu: In 1 hour, Today 15:00, Tomorrow 09:00. The row then shows the reminder time.
When due: a toast 'Reminder: …' with View; a push if the app is not open; the Later badge rises; the row moves to the top labelled 'Reminder due'.
Tick the box: the row moves to Completed, struck through.
cases: It can also be set from a message's More menu: 'Remind me about this' saves and schedules in one step.
The source message was deleted: the row reads 'Message deleted' and can still be completed or removed; the count still matches.
In Pause or Focus when due: no toast or push; the badge still rises and the item counts in the summary at the end.
Later is personal; nobody else sees it.

flows.title: Ctrl+K
flows.context: On any screen.
steps: Press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) or the Search field. The palette opens in the middle of the screen.
Before typing: recent conversations and quick actions.
While typing: results grouped as Conversations, People, Channels you can join, Messages (from 2 characters), Actions. Exact matches come first.
Arrow keys choose, Enter opens, Esc closes.
Choosing a message opens its conversation at that message; choosing a person opens their profile.
cases: Phase 1 quick actions: Create channel, Browse channels, New message, Set status, Pause notifications, Start Focus time, Switch look, and Go to Activity, Later, Files, People, Preferences.
Messages are searched only in conversations you belong to.
No results: 'No results for …'.
Narrow screens: opened from the search field at the top of Home and from the More sheet.

flows.title: The Files section
flows.context: Press Files.
steps: It shows every file, image and link from conversations you can see, newest first.
Search by file name or sender. Chips: All, Images, Documents, Links. A switch between list and grid.
Pressing a file opens the detail modal described in F18.
cases: Nothing matches: 'No files match' and a 'Clear filters' button.
Files in a private channel never appear to people outside it.

flows.title: People and profiles
flows.context: Press People.
steps: A grid of cards: avatar, presence, name, an Owner or Admin label, job title, local time. A field searches by name or job title.
Press a card, or a name or avatar on any message: the Profile panel opens on the right.
The profile: large avatar, name, job title, presence in words, status if any, local time, time zone as a UTC offset.
'Message' opens the DM. 'Start a Meet' arrives in phase 4.
Your own profile has 'Set status' and 'Edit profile'.
cases: Deactivated people are not in People; a profile opened from their old messages is labelled 'Deactivated' and has no Message button.
Nobody matches: 'Nobody matches', centred in the content area.

flows.title: Status
flows.context: Account menu → 'Set status'.
steps: The modal has 5 presets (In a meeting, Focusing, Out for lunch, Commuting, Working remotely), a free-text field, and 'Clear after': never, 30 minutes, 1 hour, end of today.
Save: the account card shows the status in place of the role. Toast: 'Status saved · clears at 14:00'.
Others see the status in the DM header, the profile, the mention popup and the People card.
When the time comes the status disappears, with a toast, 'Your status was cleared'.
cases: Saving an empty field clears the status.
A status is at most 100 characters.
Starting Focus time sets the status to 'Focusing'; ending it restores the earlier status.

flows.title: Pause notifications and Focus time
flows.context: The account menu.
steps: Choose Pause notifications (30 minutes, 1 hour, until tomorrow 08:00) or Focus time (25 minutes, 1 hour).
A strip at the top of the main area reads 'Notifications paused until 14:00 · 58:20 left' with a 'Resume' button. The account card shows a countdown.
Focus time does two more things: presence becomes Do not disturb (red dot) and the status becomes 'Focusing'.
Meanwhile: no toast, no push, no sound. Badges and Activity still update.
At the end: a toast, 'Notifications are back on · 4 things arrived while paused', with a button to open Activity.
cases: Someone opening a DM with you sees '… has paused notifications until 14:00'.
Starting Focus during Focus extends the end time; it does not nest.
Focus ends while a longer Pause is still running: notifications stay paused under that Pause.
It applies to the account, on every device.

flows.title: Automatic presence
flows.context: No action needed; Toki works it out.
steps: At least one device has Toki open and was used in the last 5 minutes: Active.
No activity for over 5 minutes, or no device connected: Away.
In Focus time: Do not disturb, whether or not there is activity.
The presence dot appears on DM rows, the DM header, profiles, People, the mention popup and member lists.
cases: 'In a Meet' arrives in phase 4.
There is no separate Offline state.
Presence cannot be set by hand; to signal busy, use a status or Focus time.

flows.title: Preferences
flows.context: Open Preferences from navigation or the account menu.
steps: Look: Calm, Focus, or Match my device. A change shows immediately without reloading.
Accent: teal, indigo, clay, violet. Density: Comfortable or Compact (hidden on narrow screens).
Notifications: Desktop notifications, Play a sound, Notify me for @mentions even in muted channels.
Language: Tiếng Việt or English. A change switches the whole interface at once.
Profile: display name, job title, time zone.
Signed-in devices (F06).
cases: Every preference is saved to the account and syncs across devices. With 'Match my device' each device follows its own light or dark setting.
The 'Email me about missed mentions' switch arrives in phase 5.

flows.title: Turn on push notifications and install the app
flows.context: First visit to Home on a device.
steps: A small card asks 'Turn on notifications so you do not miss messages?' with Turn on and Later. The browser asks for permission only after Turn on is pressed.
On approval the device is registered. A test notification appears: 'Notifications are on'.
When something needs attention and the app is closed or the tab hidden, a system notification shows the sender, the conversation and the start of the message.
Pressing the notification opens Toki at that message.
On a phone, after 'Add to Home Screen', Toki opens like an app of its own.
cases: Permission refused: Preferences shows 'Notifications are blocked in the browser' with steps to turn them back on.
On iPhone, push works only after adding to the Home Screen; Preferences explains this.
No push arrives while that very conversation is on screen.

flows.title: Losing and regaining the connection
flows.context: Using the app when the network drops.
steps: A yellow 'Reconnecting…' strip appears at the top of the main area and of the conversation list.
Loaded content can still be read and scrolled.
Messages sent now appear labelled 'Waiting to send' and go out on their own when the connection returns.
Every other write (reactions, edits, pins, joining a channel, saving settings) is locked; pressing one says 'A connection is needed'.
When the connection returns the strip goes, waiting messages are sent, what was missed is fetched, and a toast says 'Reconnected'.
cases: A drop of under 3 seconds shows no strip.
After a long absence the app reloads everything instead of only what was missed.
During a deployment the connection drops for a few seconds and recovers through this same flow.

flows.title: Getting around on a narrow screen
flows.context: A screen narrower than 720px.
steps: Bottom tabs: Home, Activity, Later, Files, More. Each has its own badge.
Home is the conversation list. Tapping a row slides the conversation in from the right, hides the tab bar, and shows a Back button in the header.
Tapping a message shows its action bar directly under the message, never over the text.
Thread, Details and Profile open full screen with a Back button.
More is a sheet with: Search, People, Preferences, Admin (with permission), and an account section with Set status, Pause notifications, Focus time, Sign out.
cases: Every control is at least 40px tall.
Toasts appear above the tab bar or the composer, never over them.

flows.title: The Admin page
flows.context: The Admin item appears in navigation only for Admins and Owners.
steps: The member table: avatar, name, email, role, status (Invited, Active, Deactivated), last active. A search field and status filter chips.
At the top: a total per status and an 'Invite members' button (F02).
Each row has an action menu whose contents depend on the viewer's role and the row's role.
cases: A Member typing /admin directly sees 'You do not have access to this page'.
Nothing on the Admin page leads to message content. Admins do not see private channels or DMs they are not in.

flows.title: Change a role
flows.context: On the Admin page, in a member's row menu.
steps: Choose 'Change role': Member, Admin, Owner.
The confirmation names the person and the new role, with a line on what changes.
Afterwards the role label updates on Admin, People and the profile. The person sees the Admin item appear or disappear at once, without signing in again.
The person gets an Activity item: 'Lan changed your role to Admin'.
cases: Admins do not see 'Change role'.
The last Owner cannot demote themselves: the entry is locked with an explanation.

flows.title: Deactivate and reactivate
flows.context: On the Admin page, in a member's row menu.
steps: Choose 'Deactivate'. The confirmation names the person and the effect: they are signed out everywhere and cannot sign in again.
On confirming, every session ends at once; the person sees 'This account has been deactivated'.
For everyone else: the person's old messages stay, their name carries a 'Deactivated' label; they leave People, mention suggestions and add-people lists; DMs with them become read-only.
'Reactivate' in the same menu lets them sign in again, back in the same channels.
cases: An Admin can deactivate Members. Only an Owner can deactivate Admins and other Owners.
Nobody can deactivate themselves. The last Owner cannot be deactivated.
There is no permanent account deletion in phase 1.

flows.title: Delete someone else's message
flows.context: In a conversation you belong to.
steps: The 'More' menu on another person's message has 'Delete'.
The confirmation names the author.
Afterwards the message becomes a line, 'Message deleted by an admin', for everyone, even when it has no replies.
The author gets an Activity item saying their message was deleted and by whom.
cases: Admins cannot edit another person's message, only delete it.
It does not apply in conversations the Admin is not in.

flows.title: Emergency access when mail cannot be sent
flows.context: Someone with access to the server.
steps: Run the admin command on the server with a member's email address.
It prints a one-time sign-in link that expires after 10 minutes.
Opening the link in a browser goes straight to Home as that account.
cases: The command refuses an email that is not in the workspace or is deactivated.
Every use is written to the server log.

flows.title: Guest: invited, then using the guest portal
flows.context: A member opens a channel's Details → 'Invite a client'.
steps: The member enters an email and an expiry date (which must be in the future). Toki sends an invitation.
The guest opens the guest sign-in page and enters their email, then the 6-digit code.
The guest sees a single screen: a 'Guest of Hugepig Studio' strip, the channel name, and three tabs, Messages, Files, Meet. There is no navigation.
The guest sends messages, reacts, replies in threads, uploads files and joins the channel's Meets.
Members see a 'Guest' label beside the guest's name everywhere, and a 'This channel has guests' strip at the top of the channel.
cases: A guest has no Message or Start a Meet button on anyone's profile, cannot create DMs, and does not see the directory.
Re-inviting the same email updates the expiry date instead of creating a second guest.

flows.title: Guest access expires
flows.context: A guest's expiry date arrives.
steps: Every session of the guest ends.
The guest sees 'Your access has expired' and a suggestion to contact the inviter.
In the channel the guest's old messages stay, and the label changes to 'Guest (expired)'.
A member extends access from the channel's Details; the guest can sign in again.

flows.title: Tasks
steps: A message's More menu → 'Turn into task': the title comes from the message; choose an assignee and a due date.
A chip appears under the message, 'Task · Alex · Thu 12 Nov'.
The Tasks section: a three-column board, To do, In progress, Done; Mine and Everyone filters; drag a card or use 'Move to'.
After creation the board shows the new card even when the current filter would hide it.

flows.title: Polls, approvals and send later
steps: The + button in the composer: Poll (a question and at least 2 options; one vote each, changeable) and Approval (choose an approver, write the request).
The approver sees a card with Approve and Decline, and an Activity item. After the decision the card records the outcome, who and when; the decision cannot be changed; the requester is told.
The arrow beside Send picks a time. A scheduled message sits above the composer with 'Send now' and 'Cancel', and carries all its attached files.

flows.title: Calendar and Meet
steps: Calendar: today's agenda and the days ahead, with week and month navigation. 'Schedule a Meet': title, channel (joined channels only), a future date and time, length, repeat, reminder.
A message with an event card is posted in the channel; the creator and admins can edit and cancel.
Join opens 5 minutes before the start. Every conversation has a Meet button in its header.
In a call: mic, camera, screen share, raise hand, reactions, two layouts, a people list, and chat kept as a thread under the 'Meet started' message.
Leaving the Meet screen during a call: a small bar floats above the composer, never over navigation. Presence becomes 'In a Meet'.
cases: A guest can join only the Meets of the channel they were invited to.

flows.title: Automations and Analytics
steps: A channel's Details → Add automation from a template: daily standup prompt, welcome new members, weekly reminder. Set the time, the message, and the placeholders {name}, {channel}, {date}.
An automation posts as 'Toki Automations' with an Automation label. It can be run now, switched on or off, and edited; deleting asks for confirmation.

The Admin page gains an Analytics tab: active people, messages, files, call minutes; a messages-per-day chart for 7, 30 or 90 days; busiest channels. Totals only, no ranking of individuals; private channels are merged into one unnamed row.

flows.title: Summaries by Claude
flows.context: Desktop app only, when Claude is installed and signed in on the computer and the switch in Preferences is on.
steps: A channel with unread messages shows 'Catch up · 8 new'. The result has What happened, Decisions and Waiting on you, each line linking to its message.
The thread panel has 'Summarise thread'. Activity has 'Catch up on everything'.
Message content goes from the user's computer to their own Claude account, not through the Toki server.
cases: Web and phone have no entry point. Read state never depends on whether a summary was made.

flows.title: Mail
steps: A Mail section with Inbox, Sent, Drafts and Archive. Read, reply, compose; archiving offers Undo.
Drafts reopen to edit and send; a reply in progress is kept per email.
'Discuss in channel' posts the email into a channel as a card.
Each channel has an email address; mail sent to it becomes a message in the channel (phase 5).

decisions.question: What do you want to build from this prototype: a real product that runs in production, a front end on mock data for demos, or a heavily cut first version?
decisions.options: (a) Real product · (b) Front end on mock data · (c) Heavily cut MVP
decisions.decision: (a) A real product, built in phases

decisions.question: The prototype holds 14 feature groups. Which of them must be in the first release?
decisions.options: Pick from the prototype's 14 feature groups
decisions.decision: Core chat, Activity, Later, Files, People, Preferences, command palette

decisions.question: The prototype shows a Desktop app, Web and Phone. Which platforms does the first release need?
decisions.options: (a) Responsive web · (b) Web + desktop · (c) Web + desktop + mobile
decisions.decision: (a) Responsive web first

decisions.question: Does one installation of Toki serve one company on its own server, or does one system serve many companies like Slack?
decisions.options: (a) Single-tenant self-hosted · (b) Multi-tenant SaaS
decisions.decision: (a), keeping workspace_id in the schema

decisions.question: Do you or your team have any technology constraints: language, framework, database, cloud?
decisions.options: Any constraints
decisions.decision: TypeScript, React, Postgres, WebSocket

decisions.question: Real video calling is the heaviest subsystem in the prototype. Self-host an open-source media server, use a hosted service, only link out to Google Meet or Zoom, or drop it from the roadmap?
decisions.options: (a) Self-hosted SFU · (b) Hosted service · (c) Link out to Google Meet · (d) Drop
decisions.decision: (a) Self-hosted LiveKit, in its own phase

decisions.question: The Mail tab looks like a personal mailbox with Inbox, Sent and Drafts. Is the intent a full email client connected to each person's Gmail or Outlook, only email into a channel, or nothing?
decisions.options: (a) Client connected to Gmail/Outlook · (b) Email-into-channel only · (c) Drop
decisions.decision: A Gmail-like interface where Toki itself sends and receives; no connection to Gmail; read and unread state. Later phase

decisions.question: The prototype says summaries are made by 'Claude on this computer', only in the desktop app, with nothing passing through the Toki server. Keep that model, have the server call the Claude API with a company key, or decide later?
decisions.options: (a) Claude on the user's computer · (b) Server calls the API · (c) Later
decisions.decision: (a), built after the desktop app exists

decisions.question: Who uses the first version, your own company or paying customers, and roughly how many people per workspace and online at once?
decisions.options: Internal or for sale; how many people
decisions.decision: Internal first, up to about 200 people, one server

decisions.question: Who will build this, you alone with Claude or a team, and is there a deadline for the first release?
decisions.options: Who builds; any deadline
decisions.decision: You alone, with Claude

decisions.question: The prototype has no sign-in screen for members, only the guest one. How do members sign in, and how are accounts created?
decisions.options: (a) Password · (b) Emailed code · (c) Google SSO
decisions.decision: (b) 6-digit emailed code, no password, admin invitation only, 30-day session

decisions.question: The prototype shows Owner, Admin and ordinary members but no difference between them. Who is allowed to do what?
decisions.options: What Member, Admin and Owner can do
decisions.decision: As in the capability table under Roles & States

decisions.question: Is there a time limit on editing a message, and what happens when a message that has a thread is deleted? The prototype deletes every reply too.
decisions.options: Time limit; deleting a message that has a thread
decisions.decision: Edit without limit; soft delete that keeps the thread

decisions.question: Where are files stored, what is the size limit, and which previews are built: image thumbnails, PDFs, link previews?
decisions.options: (a) Server disk · (b) S3 storage; size limit; previews
decisions.decision: (b) MinIO, 100 MB, image thumbnails, link previews

decisions.question: Ctrl+K searches conversations, people, messages and actions, and Vietnamese has to match when typed without diacritics. Use Postgres full-text search, or add a separate search engine?
decisions.options: (a) Postgres full-text · (b) Meilisearch
decisions.decision: (a), ignoring Vietnamese diacritics, respecting permissions

decisions.question: The prototype has desktop notifications, sound, missed-mention email, per-channel levels, mute, Pause and Focus time. Which of these are in phase 1?
decisions.options: Pick from the prototype's kinds
decisions.decision: Badges, Web Push, sound, per-channel level, mute, Pause, Focus time. Missed-mention email later

decisions.question: Which message features are in phase 1 and which wait? And what about three things the prototype does not have: @channel, a full emoji picker, and group DMs with several people?
decisions.options: What is in, what waits, and three items not in the prototype
decisions.decision: As recommended; add @channel, group DMs up to 8, keep 8 fixed emoji

decisions.question: The prototype has two looks that differ in layout as well as colour, and two languages of which only the navigation is translated. Does phase 1 build both looks and both languages, and which language is the default?
decisions.options: One look or two; one language or two
decisions.decision: Both Calm and Focus; full vi and en, Vietnamese by default

decisions.question: Is this prototype the only design source, or is there a Figma file or a requirements document as well? How closely should it be followed?
decisions.options: Prototype only, or also Figma
decisions.decision: The prototype is the only source; Claude decides what it does not draw

decisions.question: Where does the server run and who can reach it: a private network only, or the public internet on its own domain?
decisions.options: (a) Private network only · (b) Public
decisions.decision: (b) Public, Docker Compose on one VPS

decisions.question: In what order should the phases after phase 1 come? Do you want to move, merge or split any of them?
decisions.options: A seven-phase roadmap
decisions.decision: As recommended; the phone app was later moved up to phase 3

decisions.question: For the Mail phase: mail only between Toki members, or real mail where each person has an address on the company domain and writes to anyone outside?
decisions.options: (a) Between members only · (b) With anyone outside
decisions.decision: (b) as recommended; details wait for the Mail phase

decisions.question: How should the work be run: where the repository lives, whether there is CI, how much testing, and how changes are reviewed?
decisions.options: Hosting, CI, test depth, review
decisions.decision: Private GitHub, CI, test-first backend, Playwright, one PR per task group

decisions.question: You want web, desktop and phone to be built later without changing technology. Which interface technology should be shared across them?
decisions.options: P1 React + wrappers · P2 React + React Native · P3 React Native everywhere · P4 Flutter
decisions.decision: P2: React for web and desktop, React Native for phone

decisions.question: How should the backend be organised, and why Node rather than Python, including the case where an AI chatbot is added later?
decisions.options: Modular monolith in Node · Next.js · Sync platform · Python
decisions.decision: Modular monolith in Node and TypeScript; no Python

decisions.topic: When to build the phone app
decisions.question: Now that the phone app will be React Native: does phase 1 build only the web app with the groundwork laid, or the web and phone apps side by side?
decisions.options: (a) Web first with the groundwork laid · (b) Both in phase 1
decisions.decision: (a) Web first

decisions.question: Sign-in by emailed code needs the server to send mail from phase 1. Which service should send it, and do you already have a domain?
decisions.options: Resend, Postmark, SES, a Google account, self-hosted
decisions.decision: Phase 1 sends through configurable SMTP. A dedicated service is decided in a later phase

decisions.question: A fresh installation has no accounts. How does the first Owner come to exist?
decisions.options: First-run setup page, or environment
decisions.decision: Created from environment variables or seed; that admin invites members

decisions.question: What do people who join a channel later see of its history, and what happens to a channel that is no longer used?
decisions.options: What newcomers see; what happens to unused channels
decisions.decision: Full history; channels are archived, never deleted

decisions.question: On an iPhone, push notifications work only when the web app has been added to the Home Screen. Should the web app be an installable PWA?
decisions.options: Make it a PWA or not
decisions.decision: Installable PWA; service worker for push only

decisions.question: Should the prototype's sample data (Hugepig Studio, 8 people, the sample channels and messages) be used as seed data?
decisions.options: Seed the prototype's data or not
decisions.decision: Yes, for development and tests; production starts empty

decisions.question: The mail service decision was postponed, but sign-in by code depends on sending mail. How do people sign in during phase 1?
decisions.options: (a) Password · (b) Admin-issued link · (c) Keep emailed codes
decisions.decision: Withdrawn. Q11 stands: emailed codes

questions.question: Can a guest message members directly or start a Meet with them?
questions.answer: No. A guest stays inside the invited channel: no Message or Start a Meet button on profiles, no DMs, and only that channel's Meets. The server refuses any access outside the channel, with a dedicated permission test suite for guests.

questions.question: After leaving a private channel, can a member rejoin alone or do they need an invitation?
questions.answer: A member must invite them back. The leave confirmation says so; Undo is still offered for 5 seconds. Private channels never appear in Browse or Ctrl+K for outsiders. If the last member leaves, the channel is archived.

questions.question: What marks a channel as read on Web and Phone, and when does the New divider clear?
questions.answer: Read state never depends on AI. A conversation is read when it is open, the window is in use, and the person is at the bottom of the list. The New divider anchors to the first unread message at the time of opening (by ID, so it does not drift), stays while viewing, and is gone the next time the conversation opens. Opening the app or a conversation with unread messages scrolls to the divider.

questions.question: Which features must reach the phone at launch?
questions.answer: All of phase 1. On narrow screens, global search, the account menu, status, Pause and Focus time live in the More sheet; Mark done and Snooze in Activity are always visible. AI summaries exist nowhere in phase 1.

questions.question: What is the smallest supported window, and should the thread panel overlay the chat below some width?
questions.answer: Smallest is 360 × 560. From 720 to 1099px side panels overlay the chat. See rule NR2.

questions.question: How far ahead does Calendar show, and may a scheduled Meet be edited, cancelled or set in the past?
questions.answer: Any distance ahead, by moving week or month. The creator and admins can edit and cancel; changes are posted to the channel. A start time in the past is rejected. After scheduling, Calendar jumps to that Meet's day.

questions.question: What happens when a guest's access expires, and what does a repeat invitation do?
questions.answer: On expiry every guest session is revoked, the guest cannot sign in, and old messages stay with an 'expired' label; a member can extend access. Re-inviting the same email in the same channel updates the expiry instead of creating a second guest. A past expiry date is rejected; the year is always shown.

questions.question: Can a member start a Meet in a channel they have not joined?
questions.answer: No. Pickers list only joined conversations. See rule NR11.

questions.question: Should @mention suggest only channel members? What if a non-member is mentioned?
questions.answer: It suggests only members of that conversation, guests included, plus @channel. People outside the conversation are not suggested and not notified; to involve them, add them to the channel.

questions.question: After an approval decision, who is notified, and can the approver change their mind?
questions.answer: The requester gets an Activity item. The approver is not notified of their own action, and the 'asked you to approve' item becomes done. The decision is final; to change it the requester sends a new request.

questions.question: Which actions queue while offline and which are blocked?
questions.answer: Phase 1 has no offline mode: per rule NR13 only messages wait and resend. Phase 6 also queues reactions, edits, read markers and saves to Later. Always blocked offline: sending mail, joining a Meet, uploading files, inviting people, admin actions.

questions.question: What is the standard pattern for destructive actions?
questions.answer: One or the other, depending on whether the action can be reversed. See rules NR3 and NR4. Undo: archive an email, mark done, leave a public channel, remove from Later, unpin. Confirm: delete a message, delete an automation, deactivate a member, archive a channel, cancel a Meet.

questions.question: Is Mail a full client or a light reader for discussing email in channels?
questions.answer: A full client, per Q7 and Q22. Drafts reopen to edit, send or delete; there is an Archive folder; reply drafts are kept per email; folder counts are all the same kind of number; each folder has its own empty state.

questions.question: Do reminders and calendar alerts break through Pause and Focus time?
questions.answer: No. Everything is held until it ends. See rule NR6.

questions.question: How much of the interface must be in Vietnamese for the first release?
questions.answer: All of it, per Q18. CI fails when a string lacks a translation in either language.

questions.question: Which roles can open Admin and manage automations?
questions.answer: The Admin page: Admin and Owner, per Q12. Analytics: Admin and Owner. A channel's automations: Admin, Owner and the channel's creator can create and edit; only Admin and Owner see the list of all automations.

questions.question: Why are the Claude summaries desktop-only, and is a Web or Phone version planned?
questions.answer: Because per Q8 summaries run through Claude on the user's own computer, which needs the desktop app. Under that model there is no Web or Phone version. Having one would mean running AI on the server, which belongs to the open item on an AI chatbot in phase 6. On Web and Phone the interface shows no AI entry point, and read state never depends on AI.

blocks.text: The life of one message

items: The person presses send. The client generates the message ID, shows the message at once, and calls the API.
The app server checks the session and membership, stores the message, updates stored counters, and records an event.
The realtime module pushes that event to every open connection of the conversation's members.
The activity module creates items for anyone mentioned; the notifications module weighs channel level, mute, Pause and Focus, and queues a push for people who do not have the app open.
Slow work (thumbnails, link previews, the push itself) is queued; when the worker finishes, one more event updates the message.

blocks.text: Scaling path

One server is enough for the target of 200 people. If that changes, the app server runs as several copies behind Caddy, with events fanned out between copies through Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY. The design leaves that seam in place and does not switch it on.

boxes.title: Three boundary rules, enforced by lint
items: Server modules call each other only through public interfaces, never each other's tables.
`client-core` touches no DOM or browser API, so React Native can reuse it.

Components reach platform features only through `platform`. Lint bans direct use of the notification, storage, service worker and audio APIs in `ui-web`; file picking cannot be caught by lint and relies on review.

boxes.title: Four things the server does now for React Native later
items: Two session kinds: cookie for web, header token for apps.
A versioned API (`/api/v1`); within a version, fields are only added.
Multi-channel push: Web Push in phase 1, APNs and FCM plug in later.
A devices table: several devices per person, each with a kind and a push address.

blocks.text: Server modules

`auth` · `workspace` · `members` · `conversations` · `messages` · `reactions` · `files` · `search` · `activity` · `later` · `notifications` · `presence` · `realtime` · `jobs`. Later phases add `tasks`, `calendar`, `meet`, `guests`, `automations`, `mail`, `ai` without changing existing modules.
Stack
Node 22, TypeScript, Fastify, Drizzle, Zod, Postgres 17, pg-boss, MinIO, React, Vite, TanStack Router and Query, Vitest, Playwright, Caddy.
Why these choices

items: **React for web, React Native for phone:** best phone quality; all non-visual logic is shared. Phase 1 builds web only and lays the shared packages.

**Modular monolith in Node:** one thing to deploy, one language end to end, and the data contract is a shared package. One Node process holds thousands of WebSocket connections, far more than 200 people need.
**No Python:** calling a language model is an HTTP stream, which Node handles well. A Python worker can be added beside the monolith later if local models or document processing require it.
**Postgres for everything:** data, full-text search and the job queue, so there is no Redis or search engine to run.

head: Group
Tables
Main content
rows: Role, status, time zone, language, status text, Pause and Focus; hashed codes; sessions; push devices
Kind, private flag, archive time; read pointer, notification level, mute, star
Roots and replies in one table; stored reply count; search column; client-generated ID
Storage location, thumbnail; an attachment kind that later phases extend
Mentions, threads, reactions; read, done, snoozed; reminders
A numbered event log, pruned after 7 days

items: Unread is one pointer per person per conversation: "read up to this message". Thread replies do not count toward a channel's unread.
Threads are one level deep. The root author, repliers and mentioned people follow the thread automatically.
DMs and group DMs have a unique key built from the member list, so duplicates cannot be created.
Delete is a soft delete; a message with replies leaves a "deleted" line and keeps its thread.
Every table carries `workspace_id` to keep a path to multi-tenant. IDs are UUIDv7.
History is kept indefinitely. Presence is held in memory, not in the database.

sections.title: API and realtime
sections.intro: REST for every read and write. WebSocket only for the server to push events, plus the "typing" signal.

items: **Reconnect:** the client remembers the last event number, sends it on reconnect, and the server returns what was missed. After more than 7 days away, the client reloads.
**No duplicate sends:** the client generates the message ID; resending the same ID returns the stored message.
**Permissions:** checked on the server for every request. Private conversations and DMs are visible only to members, including through search, file lists and direct links.
**Files:** uploaded and downloaded through short-lived signed URLs, bypassing Node.

**Abuse limits:** rate-limited code requests; a code is cancelled after 5 wrong tries; the sign-in page never reveals which emails are members; link previews refuse internal addresses; message content is never rendered as raw HTML.
**Background jobs:** thumbnails, link previews, mail, Web Push, reminders, snooze returns, status expiry, ending Pause and Focus, pruning old data.
**Real paths** instead of the prototype's hashes: `/c/:id`, `/c/:id/t/:messageId`, `/activity`, `/later`, `/files`, `/people`, `/prefs`, `/admin`, `/login`.

**Three layouts, one component set:** Calm (wide sidebar), Focus (icon rail plus a conversation column), and narrow under 720px (bottom tabs, More sheet). Between 720 and 1099px side panels overlay the chat.
**Styling:** the prototype's CSS carried over almost intact, on CSS variables. No Tailwind, no runtime styling library.
**Self-hosted fonts:** Be Vietnam Pro, Bricolage Grotesque, JetBrains Mono, subset to Latin and Vietnamese.
**State:** server data in the `client-core` cache; interface state in the URL; transient state in components.
**Unbuilt sections are hidden:** Mail, Calendar, Meet and Tasks do not appear in navigation in phase 1.
**Screens the prototype did not draw:** sign-in, loading skeletons, the reconnecting strip, failed sends, upload progress, 404, no access, expired session.

The first admin and the #general channel are created from environment variables when the database is empty.
Mail goes through configurable SMTP. Development uses Mailpit.

plan.phasesIntro: The product is delivered in phases. Each phase ends with something people can use. Only phase 1 is broken down further.
plan.milestonesIntro: Phase 1 is delivered in six milestones. A milestone is a point where the build can be shown working. Each has a goal and an exit check; it is done when the exit check passes, not when its tickets are closed. Under each milestone are its intents: the outcomes it delivers, each to be written up as an `intent.md` and then a `spec.md`.
notes: After M3 two browsers can chat for real. That is the earliest point worth putting on a test server for daily use by a few people.
Seed data (TOKI-081) is built at the end of M3 rather than in M6, so that from then on a reset can be followed by `dev:seed` to get people, channels and messages to work with.
M1 comes before M2 so that every later screen is assembled from components that already match the prototype.
The job queue ticket (TOKI-064) sits at the start of M4 because status timers, thumbnails and link previews need it.
The intent list is a draft. Intents I16 and I17 were added on request; each has one ticket by decision.
plan.ticketsIntro: Within each milestone, tickets are grouped by work area. Codes in the Scope column (NR, OQ, G, F) point to rules, review answers, assumptions and flows in the other tabs. The last column lists questions that remain for the spec. Sizes compare tickets with each other: S about half a working session with Claude, M about one, L several.

roadmap.outro: Only phase 1 has a detailed plan. Each later phase is brainstormed on its own when its turn comes, starting from the requirements already recorded for it in Questions & Gaps and in the outline flows.

sections.title: User flows
sections.intro: Each chart follows one person through one situation and branches at every question the system asks: is there a session, is the link still valid, what is the role. A diamond is a question; the arrows leaving it carry the answers. The accent outline is where a flow starts, a filled pill is where it ends well, and a red outline is a refusal or a dead end. These charts show the product's decided behaviour. The prototype has no sign-in for members, so charts 1 to 5 come from the decisions recorded in this Blueprint rather than from the prototype.

spec.intro: Each chart follows one person through one situation and branches at every question the system asks: is there a session, is the link still valid, what is the role. A diamond is a question; the arrows leaving it carry the answers. The accent outline is where a flow starts, a filled pill is where it ends well, and a red outline is a refusal or a dead end.
